result.topic_en: Part of Ramanujan's work on highly composite-type numbers for the divisor function sigma_{-s}(N): taking phi(x) = log((1-x^{-s(r+1)})/(1-x^{-sr})) in a partial-summation formula, he obtains an upper bound for sigma_{-s}(N), determines the epsilon that minimises it, and introduces the function Sigma_{-s}(N).

62. In (16) let us suppose that
$\phi(x) = \log \frac{1 - x^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - x^{-sr}}$.
Then we see that
$\log \Pi_r(x_r) = \pi(x_r) \log \frac{1 - x_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - x_r^{-sr}} - \int \pi(x_r)\, d\left(\log \frac{1 - x_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - x_r^{-sr}}\right)$
$= \pi(x_r) \log(x_r^{\epsilon}) - \int \pi(x_r)\, d(\log x_r^{\epsilon})$
$= \epsilon\, \pi(x_r) \log x_r - \int \pi(x_r) \log x_r\, d\epsilon - \int \frac{\epsilon\, \pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r$
in virtue of (319). Hence
(320) $\log \Pi_r(x_r) - \epsilon\, \vartheta(x_r) = \epsilon \{ \pi(x_r) \log x_r - \vartheta(x_r) \} - \int \pi(x_r) \log x_r\, d\epsilon - \int \frac{\epsilon\, \pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r$
$= \epsilon \int \frac{\pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r - \int \pi(x_r) \log x_r\, d\epsilon - \int \frac{\epsilon\, \pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r$
$= \int d\epsilon \int \frac{\pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r - \int \pi(x_r) \log x_r\, d\epsilon$
$= \int \left\{ \int \frac{\pi(x_r)}{x_r} dx_r - \pi(x_r) \log x_r \right\} d\epsilon$
$= - \int \vartheta(x_r)\, d\epsilon$
It follows from (318) and (320) that
(321) $\sigma_{-s}(N) \leq N^{\epsilon} e^{- \int \{ \vartheta(x_1) + \vartheta(x_2) + \vartheta(x_3) + \cdots \} d\epsilon}$
for all values of N. By arguments similar to those of §38 we can show that the right-hand side of (321) is a minimum when $\epsilon$ is a function of N defined by the equation
(322) $N = e^{\vartheta(x_1) + \vartheta(x_2) + \vartheta(x_3) + \cdots}$
Now let $\Sigma_{-s}(N)$ be a function of N defined by the equation
(323) $\Sigma_{-s}(N) = \Pi_1(x_1) \Pi_2(x_2) \Pi_3(x_3) \cdots$
